output.answer: Yes. T-Mobile has announced and is carrying out multiple rounds of layoffs. Its U.S. headcount fell by 4,671 jobs in the first half of 2026 — from 70,036 at Dec. 31, 2025 to 65,365 at June 30, 2026 (a 6.7% reduction), per parent Deutsche Telekom's interim report — under CEO Srini Gopalan's restructuring to centralize teams and cut duplicative roles. Separately, WARN filings show 393 Washington-state layoffs in February 2026 and another 77 (63 new plus 14 deferred) at Bellevue headquarters, retail stores and remote roles between Sept. 21 and Nov. 18, 2026, with six retail locations closing.
caveats: T-Mobile has not announced a single company-wide layoff number for 2026; the 4,671 headcount decline is from Deutsche Telekom's interim report and includes attrition, timing of workforce-transformation moves and UScellular-acquisition-related redundancies, not only announced layoffs. T-Mobile's own statement notes its employee count actually increased in the 2025 10-K due to acquisitions.

T-Mobile frames the changes as ongoing resource reallocation and a retail-footprint evolution toward fewer, company-owned stores rather than a formal mass-layoff program; totals from state WARN notices cover only states that require such filings (e.g., the Washington figures), so nationwide totals are not disclosed.
Further cuts or store closures could be announced at any time; the latest confirmed earnings context is Q3 2026 results published Oct. 28, 2026.

passages.quote:
The Bellevue, Washington-based operator reduced its headcount by a whopping 4,671 positions in the U.S. since the first of the year, according to an [interim report filed last week by parent Deutsche Telekom](https://www.telekom.com/en/investor-relations/publications/financial-results) (DT). 

T-Mobile’s U.S. headcount stood at 65,365 as of June 30, 2026, a 6.7% reduction from the December 31, 2025, total of 70,036.

T-Mobile CEO Srini Gopalan, who [took over from Mike Sievert in November](https://www.fierce-network.com/wireless/t-mobile-names-srini-gopalan-ceo), is overseeing the latest round of cuts, which began in the fourth quarter of 2025. 

That’s when the company started to implement a restructuring initiative to “streamline operations by centralizing leaders and teams, reducing organizational layers, and eliminating duplicative roles,” according to [an SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1283699/000119312526182029/d43081dars.pdf). 

During 2025, the company recorded a pre-tax charge of $390 million related to the 2025 “Workforce Transformation,” with substantially all associated employee separations and related cash outflows expected to be complete in 2026.

T-Mobile is cutting 77 jobs across Washington state, trimming staff across its Bellevue headquarters, regional retail stores, and remote roles, according to a new state filing.

The layoffs are expected to occur between Sept. 21 and Nov. 18, according to the [Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification](https://esd.wa.gov/employer-requirements/layoffs-and-employee-notifications/worker-adjustment-and-retraining-notification-warn-layoff-and-closure-database) from the Washington Employment Security Department.

The workforce reductions span frontline, regional, and corporate roles, eliminating positions ranging from retail mobile experts and account care specialists to principal systems architects and senior directors at the wireless carrier.

In addition to 63 newly disclosed job cuts, the filing includes 14 workers whose previously announced departures were deferred to this fall.

The strong earnings come against a backdrop of sustained job cuts. T-Mobile's U.S. headcount fell from 70,036 at the end of 2025 to 65,365 as of June 30, a reduction of 4,671 positions, the [Downtown Bellevue Network reported](https://downtownbellevue.com/2026/08/26/t-mobile-to-lay-off-77-workers-across-washington-including-in-bellevue) in August, citing parent company Deutsche Telekom's second-quarter report.

In August, a state WARN notice showed T-Mobile planned to permanently lay off 77 more employees at eight Washington locations, including Bellevue, with separations beginning Sept. 21.

That followed 393 Washington layoffs earlier in the year.

key_facts.fact: T-Mobile's U.S. headcount fell by 4,671 positions in the first half of 2026, from 70,036 at Dec. 31, 2025 to 65,365 as of June 30, 2026 (a 6.7% reduction), according to Deutsche Telekom's interim report.

The cuts stem from a restructuring launched in Q4 2025 to 'streamline operations by centralizing leaders and teams, reducing organizational layers, and eliminating duplicative roles' (per an SEC filing); T-Mobile recorded a $390 million pre-tax charge in 2025 for its 2025 'Workforce Transformation,' with substantially all separations expected to be complete in 2026. CEO Srini Gopalan, who took over from Mike Sievert in November 2025, is overseeing the cuts.

A Washington-state WARN notice shows T-Mobile is cutting 77 jobs across Washington state — 63 newly disclosed plus 14 deferred — spanning Bellevue headquarters, regional retail stores and remote roles, with layoffs occurring Sept. 21 to Nov. 18, 2026, and permanent closures of retail stores in Seattle, Bothell, Kennewick, Tacoma, Vancouver and Yakima.
T-Mobile previously cut 393 workers in Washington state in February 2026.

T-Mobile reported a 27% net income jump and raised its 2026 outlook (Q3 results published Oct. 28, 2026), even as sustained job cuts continued; headcount fell 4,671 positions in H1 2026 per Deutsche Telekom's Q2 report.
